key_insight: CAHP reframes attention head pruning as a global graph-based selection problem, preserving complementary heads instead of ranking heads independently.
engineering_relevance: It offers a post-hoc compression method for Transformers that can improve deployment efficiency without requiring a preset pruning ratio or extensive manual tuning.
method: Build a graph over attention heads using information-theoretic distance measures.
Cluster heads to select a topologically diverse, complementary subset.
Automatically stop pruning when the marginal performance drop becomes sharp, based on a polynomial-fit criterion.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on SST-5 and MNLI across multiple Transformer scales, where it outperformed competitive baselines, especially at high compression.
watch_item: The automatic stopping rule depends on the chosen polynomial degree, so results may be sensitive to that implementation choice.
paper_title: Complementary Attention Head Pruning for Efficient Transformers
